Build a Multilevel Vector Autoregression (mlVAR) network

Source: R/mlvar.R
build_mlvar.Rd

build_mlvar() fits a multilevel vector autoregression to intensive longitudinal panel data (ESM or EMA: many people, each measured on many occasions) and returns its three networks. The temporal network is directed and holds the fixed-effect lagged regression coefficients: the weight in row i, column j is the coefficient of variable i at an earlier occasion on variable j now, so each edge runs from the earlier variable to the one it predicts. The contemporaneous network is undirected: the partial correlations of the within-person residuals at the same occasion. The between-subjects network is undirected too: the partial correlations of the person means. Each variable is regressed, in a mixed model, on every variable lag occasions earlier and on the other variables' person means; the temporal and contemporaneous effects are fixed and only the intercepts are random.

The temporal and contemporaneous edges describe within-person relations averaged over people; the between-subjects edges describe how people who differ in one variable on average differ in another (Epskamp et al., 2018). Only random intercepts are estimated, so the networks do not show how people differ in their dynamics. A temporal edge is a lagged predictive association, and a contemporaneous edge has no temporal order. coefs() gives each temporal coefficient with its standard error, p-value and confidence interval; check them before interpreting any single temporal edge.

Usage

build_mlvar(
  data,
  vars,
  id,
  day = NULL,
  beep = NULL,
  lag = 1L,
  standardize = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'net_mlvar'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_mlvar'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_mlvar'
plot(x, layer = NULL, ...)

Arguments

data

The panel data: a data frame with one row per measurement occasion. A column named in vars, id, day or beep that is not in it raises an error.

vars

The columns to model, at least two.

id

The column identifying the person each row belongs to.

day

The column identifying the day (or session) of each row. When given, lagged pairs are formed only within the same day. Default NULL.

beep

The column numbering the measurement occasions. When NULL (default), the row position within each person (and day) is used.

lag

How many occasions back the predictors of the temporal network are, a whole number of at least 1: lag = 2 regresses each variable on every variable two occasions earlier (that lag only, not lags 1 and 2). Default 1.

standardize

Whether to grand-mean centre each variable and divide it by its pooled SD before the panel is augmented, as mlVAR::mlVAR(scale = TRUE) does. Default FALSE, matching mlVAR::mlVAR(scale = FALSE) (mlVAR's own default is TRUE); FALSE is the only setting for which agreement with mlVAR has been validated.

x

For the print() method: a net_mlvar.

...

For the print() and summary() methods: not used.

object

For the summary() method: a net_mlvar.

layer

For the plot() method: "temporal", "contemporaneous" or "between" to draw that network alone. Default NULL draws all three side by side.

Value

A net_mlvar object (class c("net_mlvar", "netobject_group")): a named list of three networks, with the model-level results stored as attributes. print() gives the number of subjects, observations and variables, the lag, and how many temporal edges are significant; coefs() returns the temporal coefficients, one row per outcome and predictor; summary() prints the three weight matrices and the significant temporal edges and returns the same table as coefs(), visibly, so at the console the matrices are followed by the table. idiographic registers its own print() and summary() methods for net_mlvar; Nestimate loads it first and registers its methods after, so these two are the ones that run. Each network is a netobject (class c("netobject", "cograph_network")) built from its weight matrix, without data; the Dispatch limitation section lists the verbs that do not work on it. The parts:

temporal

Directed network of the d x d matrix of fixed-effect lagged coefficients: the weight in row i, column j is the effect of variable i at t - lag on variable j at t, so edges run from predictor to outcome. Method "mlvar_temporal".

contemporaneous

Undirected d x d network of the partial correlations of the within-person lmer residuals. Method "mlvar_contemporaneous".

between

Undirected d x d network of the partial correlations of the person means, derived from D (I - Gamma). Method "mlvar_between".

coefficient table (attribute coefs)

The data frame coefs() returns: one row per (outcome, predictor) pair, with columns outcome, predictor, beta, se, t, p, ci_lower, ci_upper and significant.

attribute n_obs

The number of rows of the augmented panel after rows with missing values are removed.

attribute n_subjects

The number of subjects remaining.

attribute lag

The lag used.

attribute standardize

Whether the variables were standardised before augmentation.

The print() method returns its input invisibly.

Details

Estimation is done by idiographic::fit_mlvar(), called with estimator = "lmer", temporal = "fixed" and contemporaneous = "fixed". It follows mlVAR's lmer path:

  1. Drop rows with NA in id/day/beep and, with standardize = TRUE, grand-mean standardise each variable.

  2. Expand the per-(id, day) beep grid and right-join the original values, giving the augmented panel (augData).

  3. Add within-person lagged predictors (L1_*) and person-mean predictors (PM_*).

  4. For each outcome variable fit lmer(y ~ within + between-except-own-PM + (1 | id)) with REML = FALSE. Collect the fixed-effect temporal matrix B, the between-effect matrix Gamma, the random-intercept SDs (mu_SD) and the lmer residual SDs.

  5. Contemporaneous network: cor2pcor(D %*% cov2cor(cor(resid)) %*% D).

  6. Between-subjects network: cor2pcor(pseudoinverse(forcePositive(D (I - Gamma)))).

The result agrees with mlVAR::mlVAR() to machine precision (largest difference below 1e-10) on 25 real ESM datasets from openesm and 20 simulated configurations, and exactly with the implementation Nestimate carried before 0.9.0 on all layers, coefficients and observation counts, across settings of lag, standardize, day and beep.

The temporal weight matrix has predictors in rows and outcomes in columns, the transpose of mlVAR's Beta and the same matrix as mlVAR::getNet(, "temporal"). A Nestimate network reads its weight matrix from row to column, so the edges of the temporal network (its edge list and extract_edges()) run from the predictor at t - lag to the outcome at t. Nestimate 1.0.9 and earlier did not transpose it, so every temporal edge pointed from the outcome to its predictor.

When the data carry no between-person variance (a random-intercept SD of zero), the between-subjects network cannot be estimated. Since 0.9.0 idiographic then raises a warning and the zero matrix is returned by convention; before 0.9.0 the zero matrix was returned silently.

Dispatch limitation

plot() draws the three networks side by side, or one with layer, with cograph::splot() when cograph is installed and in base graphics otherwise; each constituent can also be drawn on its own (cograph::splot() on the temporal network). The constituents are wrappers around their weight matrices and carry no data, so the verbs that resample or reread the data, bootstrap_network(), network_reliability() and centrality_stability(), raise an error on the fit and on each constituent, and certainty() refuses them as not transition networks. net_centrality() and summary() read the weights and work on each constituent. coefs() gives the model output.

Methods

  • summary.net_mlvar() prints the three weight matrices and the significant temporal edges, then returns the coefficient table of coefs().

References

Epskamp, S., Waldorp, L. J., Mõttus, R., & Borsboom, D. (2018). The Gaussian graphical model in cross-sectional and time-series data. Multivariate Behavioral Research, 53(4), 453–480. doi:10.1080/00273171.2018.1454823

See also

build_network()

Examples

# A three-variable ESM panel: 20 people x 20 beeps. `tired` is driven by
# `happy` one beep earlier, so the temporal network should recover it.
if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  n_beep <- 20
  ar1 <- function(n, phi) as.numeric(stats::filter(stats::rnorm(n), phi,
                                                   method = "recursive"))
  panel <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(20), function(i) {
    happy <- ar1(n_beep, 0.4)
    data.frame(
      id    = i,
      beep  = seq_len(n_beep),
      happy = happy + stats::rnorm(1),
      calm  = ar1(n_beep, 0.3) + stats::rnorm(1),
      tired = 0.5 * c(0, happy[-n_beep]) + stats::rnorm(n_beep) +
              stats::rnorm(1)
    )
  }))
  fit <- build_mlvar(panel, vars = c("happy", "calm", "tired"),
                     id = "id", beep = "beep")
  fit
  coefs(fit)
  summary(fit)
}
